Harbour ferries move to battery power by 2028

The city will replace its six diesel ferries with electric boats charged at both ends of each crossing.

By Lina Park · 28 September 2026

The harbour authority approved a plan on Monday to replace all six of the city's diesel ferries with battery boats by the summer of 2028. Each crossing takes under twelve minutes, short enough that the new boats will charge for a few minutes at every quay rather than carrying enough energy for a whole day.

Charging masts will go up at the south quay first, followed by the island piers. The authority says the masts draw from the same substation that already powers the quay cranes, and that the peak load of a ferry charging is below what the cranes use when they lift together, so no new cable has to be laid under the harbour.

Crews will train on the first boat through the winter. The operator plans to keep two diesel ferries in reserve until the last electric boat has run a full season, after which they will be sold. Fares do not change, and the timetable stays the same, although the authority expects fewer cancellations in fog because the new boats carry better radar.

Residents on the island piers had asked for quieter boats for years. The electric ferries are expected to cut the noise at the piers by about half, and to remove the smell of exhaust that drifts over the waiting rooms on still mornings.
